evals.name: create-new-skill-from-concrete-workflow
evals.prompt: Use skill-creator style thinking and help me make a brand new skill from scratch. I keep doing the same work turning rough incident notes into clean postmortem drafts for my team. I want a reusable skill so next time I can say things like 'turn these outage notes into a postmortem' or 'draft the incident review from this timeline.' Please create the skill package, not just a one-off answer.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger accelint-skill-manager and follow the new-skill creation path rather than only polishing prose. The response should gather 2-3 concrete clarification points first, identify reusable artifacts that belong in scripts/references/assets, mention checking for existing overlapping skills before creating a new one, and outline or create a proper skill package centered on SKILL.md plus supporting files. It should frame the description around concrete trigger phrases and keep creation guidance focused on expert reusable workflow content rather than generic tutorials.
assertions: Recognizes this as a new skill creation request and routes to the full creation workflow
Asks concrete scoping questions before drafting the skill instead of immediately writing a final SKILL.md
Identifies at least one reusable artifact candidate for references/, scripts/, or assets/
Mentions or implies overlap checking against existing skills
Produces or proposes a package-oriented outcome rather than a single prompt rewrite

evals.name: targeted-refinement-description-only
evals.prompt: Open /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-skill-manager/SKILL.md and tighten just the frontmatter description so it triggers more reliably for people asking to review or improve a skill package. Do not do a full rewrite. Keep the body structure intact and make only the smallest necessary package changes, including version/changelog handling if needed.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger accelint-skill-manager for targeted refinement, not a prose-only skill. The response should choose the lightest execution path, focus on the description/frontmatter area, avoid broad restructuring, preserve the rest of the skill body, and include version/changelog updates appropriate to a localized non-breaking change. It should use the skill's own description-field conventions and semantic-version guidance.
assertions: Recognizes this as targeted refinement rather than full creation or generic prose cleanup
Limits scope to localized package changes centered on SKILL.md frontmatter
Keeps the body structure intact instead of proposing a broad rewrite
Mentions or applies a patch-level version bump and matching CHANGELOG update
Uses trigger-oriented language in the proposed description

evals.name: audit-only-skill-package-review
evals.prompt: Please audit /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-skill-manager as a skill package and tell me what's weak. I only want an audit with prioritized findings and suggestions. Do not rewrite the skill or patch files unless I ask.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger accelint-skill-manager in audit mode. The response should follow the audit workflow: inspect frontmatter, structure, changelog/version alignment, and knowledge-delta quality; then return actionable findings ranked by priority. It should respect the audit-only constraint by not drafting replacement files unless clearly asked, though it may provide a sample improved description as part of recommendations.
assertions: Recognizes and respects the audit-only boundary
Covers frontmatter audit points including description quality and version presence
Checks structure against expected sections or package expectations
Reviews CHANGELOG/version alignment and rationale quality
Returns prioritized, actionable findings rather than silently editing files

evals.name: trigger-boundary-near-miss-prompt-polish
evals.prompt: Can you make the wording in this skill file sound less robotic? I mainly want the prose smoothed out and maybe shortened a bit, but I do not want to change the package structure or do a skill audit. Just help with the wording.
evals.expected_output: This is a trigger-boundary near miss. accelint-skill-manager should not be the preferred skill because the user is asking for prose cleanup rather than skill-package architecture or quality work. The ideal behavior is to route to a prose-oriented skill, explicitly noting that the request is mainly wording-focused and not about structural skill management.
assertions: Does not center the response on accelint-skill-manager's creation/audit workflow
Recognizes the request as prose-only cleanup rather than package-architecture work
Prefers a prose/prompt-focused skill over skill-manager
Avoids unnecessary discussion of versioning, changelog, or package structure changes

evals.name: description-optimization-request
evals.prompt: I think /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-skill-manager isn't getting invoked enough when people ask to 'review a skill' or 'fix this SKILL.md'. Optimize its trigger description and show how you'd evaluate whether the new description is actually better at activating on the right requests and staying off near misses.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger accelint-skill-manager for skill-package work with a description-optimization focus. The response should address trigger quality directly, propose stronger description language using concrete trigger phrases, and describe an eval approach with should-trigger and should-not-trigger queries rather than only making a vague rewrite. It should stay grounded in activation accuracy, especially undertriggering and near-miss boundaries.
assertions: Recognizes description optimization as in-scope skill-manager work
Proposes a revised description with explicit trigger phrases relevant to skill-package requests
Discusses evaluating trigger performance with both positive and negative/near-miss queries
Addresses undertriggering rather than only general prose quality
Keeps focus on the description field as the primary activation surface

evals.name: detect-version-changelog-mismatch
evals.prompt: Please inspect /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-skill-manager and tell me if the declared version and the changelog history are aligned. If they are not, explain the mismatch and what should be updated. If they are aligned, say so clearly and tell me what evidence you checked.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger accelint-skill-manager in audit mode with emphasis on version governance. The response should inspect SKILL.md frontmatter metadata.version and compare it to the latest CHANGELOG.md entry, then report whether they match and cite the evidence checked. If a mismatch exists it should explain the corrective action; if not, it should still explicitly confirm alignment rather than skipping the check.
assertions: Checks metadata.version in SKILL.md against the latest CHANGELOG entry
States clearly whether versions are aligned or mismatched
Provides evidence from both files rather than a guess
Explains corrective action if a mismatch is found, or explicit confirmation if aligned

evals.name: artifact-consistency-across-package-files
evals.prompt: Run a consistency review of /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-skill-manager across SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, references/, assets/skill-template/, and evals/evals.json. I want to know whether the package tells one coherent story about how to create, refine, and audit skills, or whether there are contradictions, stale instructions, or missing artifacts.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger accelint-skill-manager for package-level consistency review. The response should compare guidance across multiple artifacts, not just SKILL.md, and look for contradictions such as outdated workflow step counts, stale template guidance, missing referenced files, or eval coverage gaps. It should return a cross-file findings list that speaks to overall package coherence.
assertions: Inspects multiple package artifacts rather than only SKILL.md
Looks for cross-file contradictions or stale instructions
Mentions missing referenced artifacts if any are absent
Evaluates whether eval coverage matches the skill's stated workflows
Returns coherence findings across the package

evals.name: trigger-boundary-near-miss-readme-docs-work
evals.prompt: I need help rewriting the README for my tool and maybe generating docs pages for it. There is also a SKILL.md in the repo somewhere, but this task is really about user-facing docs and examples, not about changing the skill package itself. Which skill should handle this?
evals.expected_output: This is another trigger-boundary near miss. accelint-skill-manager should not be selected as the primary skill because the user is asking for README/docs work rather than creating, auditing, or structurally improving a skill package. The ideal behavior is to prefer a README/docs-oriented skill and explicitly explain why skill-manager is not the best fit here.
assertions: Does not choose accelint-skill-manager as the primary path
Recognizes the presence of SKILL.md as incidental to the real docs task
Prefers a README/docs-focused skill
Explains the boundary between skill-package work and general documentation work

evals.name: repair-broken-reference-paths-and-missing-artifacts
evals.prompt: I copied this skill package into a new repo and now some guidance points to files that don't exist anymore. Please inspect the whole package, find broken internal references or missing artifacts, and tell me the smallest safe set of fixes to restore integrity without doing an unnecessary rewrite.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger accelint-skill-manager for package-integrity maintenance. The response should inspect internal references and artifact existence across the skill package, identify broken links or stale references, and recommend minimal targeted fixes instead of a broad overhaul. It should treat this as skill-package maintenance, not generic docs cleanup.
assertions: Recognizes broken internal references and missing artifacts as in-scope skill-package work
Inspects package files for reference integrity rather than only one file
Prefers minimal targeted fixes over broad rewriting
Frames the outcome as restoring package coherence and usability

evals.name: near-miss-generic-prompt-improvement-request
evals.prompt: I wrote a prompt for Claude to analyze customer interviews, but it's too wordy and the results feel vague. Can you rewrite the prompt so it's clearer and more actionable, while keeping the same intent?
evals.expected_output: This should not prefer accelint-skill-manager because the real task is improving a prompt, not creating or maintaining a skill package. The ideal behavior is to route to a prompt-focused skill and avoid unnecessary package-management framing.
assertions: Does not route primarily through accelint-skill-manager
Recognizes prompt rewriting as distinct from skill-package work
Prefers a prompt-focused or prose-focused skill
Avoids discussing skill-package versioning, changelog, or file structure
